headlines.title: Colts won't move Jonathan Taylor for less than a premium haul
headlines.summary: Indianapolis is open to trading its running back but wants a first-round pick, according to Tom Pelissero. The Colts have already turned down a 2027 second-round pick plus an additional pick. Taylor is 27 and signed a two-year, $44 million extension in August. The Colts have traded Nelson and Buckner but are not in fire-sale mode. The Colts are 2-5 and 12th in the AFC South, so the call on Taylor is a big one for their direction.
headlines.whyItMatters: For now the Colts are holding out for a first-round price.

headlines.title: Derwin James goes on injured reserve and the Chargers stay winless
headlines.summary: The Chargers placed All-Pro safety Derwin James on injured reserve after a setback in his return from a hamstring injury. He has not played since Week 3. His earliest return is now Week 12, against the Patriots. Los Angeles is 0-6 after six straight losses, and it is also without guard Kayode Awosika and others for Week 8 against the Rams. Tight end David Njoku and left tackle Rashawn Slater have also been hit by injuries this season.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Chargers are the only winless team in the NFL, and the injury list is getting longer as the losing streak grows.

headlines.title: Seahawks rebuild the offensive line for Monday night against the Bears
headlines.summary: Seattle beat the Chiefs in Week 7 and hosts Chicago on Monday night. The Seahawks added six-time All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson. Left tackle Charles Cross will miss the game with an ankle injury. Josh Jones moves to left tackle and Grey Zabel slides to right guard, the first time those three have started together. Zach Charbonnet is cleared to play and Rashid Shaheed is ruled out. Chicago has added defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons, who changes what the Bears can do up front.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Seahawks are 4-3 and a half game out of the NFC playoff picture. A win over the 5-2 Bears keeps them in the race.

headlines.title: Only one of eight helmet fines came with a flag
headlines.summary: Giants running back Cam Skattebo was fined $7,073 for illegal use of the helmet in Week 7. Yahoo Sports found that the fine was not the unusual part. Of eight fines for helmet violations that week, only Skattebo's came with a flag on the field. The hit that flattened Texans safety M.J. Stewart was likely a factor.
headlines.whyItMatters: The fines show the league is punishing helmet use more often than the officials are calling it on the field.

contextCard.title: How NFL bye weeks work
contextCard.body: Each team gets one week off during the regular season, so every team plays 17 games across 18 weeks. A bye gives injured players extra time to heal and lets coaches self-scout. The Jets have their bye in Week 9, which is the week after they play the Raiders.

headlines.title: Holmgren's injury leaves the Thunder short-handed
headlines.summary: Chet Holmgren is out 8 to 10 weeks with a knee injury, according to ESPN. Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace are also set to miss extended time, so Oklahoma City has lost three key players early in the season. The Thunder are no longer signing free agent Ochai Agbaji and are reconsidering their open roster spot. Rookie Aday Mara becomes a bigger part of the rotation, and CBS Sports reports there are trade rumours swirling around the team.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Thunder are 4-1 and third in the West, but losing three players for extended time will test their depth.

headlines.title: Jeanie Buss accuses her siblings of conspiring against her
headlines.summary: In a court filing this week, Jeanie Buss accused Joey and Jesse Buss of a 'cloak and dagger' campaign through the media. She said they were jealous that their father chose her to govern the Lakers. The siblings want to sell their remaining shares to an ownership group led by Bob Iger and Josh Kushner, which is buying the team from Mark Walter at a $12.5 billion valuation. Buss has asked a judge to block the sale. A hearing is set for 8 December in Los Angeles Superior Court.
headlines.whyItMatters: A ruling on the sale would decide whether Buss keeps her role as governor of the Lakers.

headlines.title: Reed Sheppard's fourth-year option is picked up
headlines.summary: The Rockets have picked up Reed Sheppard's fourth-year option, which pays him just above $14 million for the 2027-28 season. Sheppard is the 10th first-round pick Houston has selected from 2021 to 2024, and the sixth of those 10 to have his option picked up. The previous five all signed extensions. Sheppard has moved from the outside of the rotation to Fred VanVleet's backup at point guard.
headlines.whyItMatters: Houston is signalling it wants Sheppard around for at least the next two seasons, with an extension possible after 2027.

headlines.title: Celtics open the NBA Cup with a 125-111 win over the Bulls
headlines.summary: Payton Pritchard scored 30 points to lead Boston past Chicago in the opening game of the NBA Cup. The Celtics beat the Bulls 125-111. Boston is 4-1 and has won four straight. Coach Joe Mazzulla challenged Pritchard before the game, and he delivered. The win came in the first week of the in-season tournament.
headlines.whyItMatters: Boston is 4-1 and third in the East, a strong start for a team with its eyes on the Cup.

recaps.text: The Warriors beat the Lakers 112-95 after erasing a 25-point halftime deficit, which Yahoo Sports reports no NBA team had ever done. Luka Doncic had 37 points and six threes, but Golden State's Stephen Curry scored 31 with eight threes. Austin Reaves was a big part of Los Angeles's turnover problems, and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had the worst performance of his young career after the Luka trash talk.

recaps.text: Dallas beat the 5-0 Rockets 116-111 in a game decided by five points. Kyrie Irving had 35 points, nine assists and five threes. Cooper Flagg had 33 points and nine rebounds. Houston got 28 from Kevin Durant and 22 from Jabari Smith Jr. The Mavericks have won three straight.

He said after the game he was 'more than happy' he made the decision to come to Philadelphia. Jalen Brunson had 24 and Karl-Anthony Towns had 22 and 12 rebounds for New York.
